title: V2: rows inside d.results
intro: Two orders on screen, 42 in the complete set.
context: Illustrative HTTP request/response pair at a fictional endpoint. Metadata defines Orders with an Edm.Int32 key named ID. Request and response are displayed together for comparison.

highlights.label: Request the total
highlights.explanation: V2 uses $inlinecount=allpages; V4 uses $count=true. $top=2 limits this page, not the total count.

highlights.label: Read the response
highlights.explanation: V2 uses a string __count and d.results. V4 uses a numeric @odata.count in this example and value. A V2 parser must therefore change.

outcome: The user sees the same two orders; the contract between client and service changes.
caveat: This is not a speed measurement or a working SAP endpoint. Other metadata fields are omitted. The V4 example does not enable IEEE754Compatible=true, which would serialize the count as a string. Server-driven paging may add a next link.

title: V4: the same list, a different contract
intro: Two orders on screen, 42 in the complete set.
context: Illustrative HTTP request/response pair at a fictional endpoint. Metadata defines Orders with an Edm.Int32 key named ID. Request and response are displayed together for comparison.
code:
GET /v4/Orders?$top=2&$orderby=ID&$count=true HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.test
Accept: application/json;odata.metadata=minimal

HTTP/1.1 200 OK
Content-Type: application/json;odata.metadata=minimal
OData-Version: 4.0

{
  "@odata.context": "https://api.example.test/v4/$metadata#Orders",
  "@odata.count": 42,
  "value": [
    { "ID": 7 },
    { "ID": 9 }
  ]
}
